programmes.d: Further investigation proves that a woman's suffocation after falling asleep was staged.

A mysterious computer crash pushed a thriving manufacturing company to the brink of collapse, jeopardizing hundreds of jobs. Forensic investigators had to determine if the crash was the result of a computer defect, human error, or sabotage.
A killer is careless when a home is destroyed by fire and a young boy is missing.

When Kristine Fitzhugh failed to show up for her music class, her husband found her dead at the bottom of the stairs of their Palo Alto home. Further investigation reveals evidence of murder in the kitchen.
Highway policeman is shocked when a bloody traffic collision is classified as an accident.
When a hit-and-run boating accident caused the death of a popular young man, investigators faced the daunting task of searching for one boat among 1200 others.
The decomposed body of a young woman was discovered in a Bakersfield irrigation canal.
When two boys are brutally attacked, investigators rely on evidence fished out of a nearby pond. It became the first case where diatom analysis was used to place a suspect at the scene of the crime.
A behavioral profile caused the Baton Rouge Police Department to search for the wrong man.
On May 12, 1994, Crystal Perry was viciously murdered in her home in Bridgton, Maine. Michael Hutchinson, 32, was later found guilty in the slaying.
Blood splatter evidence contradicts an obstetrician's story who found his wife dead.
A family vacation turns into a nightmare when a woman is found face-down in a lake.
A California teenager is found dead after disappearing from her home.

Just weeks before a witness is to testify against the man accused of sexually assaulting her, she is murdered in the front yard of her own home. Investigators immediately suspect her attacker, but they don't have enough evidence to prove his guilt.
Police recover the submerged car of missing man but find no body; uncovering a motive for murder.

A killer tries to incinerate everything that could link him to his crime. But in doing so, he inadvertently creates new forensic evidence. Detectives employ a technique never before used in a criminal investigation to bring it to light.
911 received a call from a man who said his girlfriend shot herself. The autopsy revealed the truth.

Casino security cameras tracked a young woman's movements until shortly before she disappeared. She was never seen again, but through the evidence she left behind, she was able to tell investigators what happened to her and who was responsible.
Police investigate a Native American woman's murder less than 10 miles from another murder scene.
In the 1990s, the media dubbed Richard Rogers the "Last Call Killer" because he targeted men in gay bars who were obviously intoxicated.
A brilliant architect became ill and died just before she was to testify in a criminal trial.
When two women went missing and were later found brutally murdered, police wondered if they were victims of a hate crime.
Eyewitnesses description don't come close to resembling the prime suspect.
Doctors don't know why a young scientist has fallen gravely ill. When tests finally reveal the cause, it's too late to save him.
The murder of an eccentric millionaire was more than just a robbery.

A behavioral profile caused the Baton Rouge Police Department to search for the wrong man. The real perpetrator may have eluded arrest, had it not been for a molecular biologist who painted DNA picture of the suspect.
Woman disappears from grocery store parking lot in Boulder; investigators find extraordinary clues.

An Alaskan police officer finds a woman's body while on routine patrol of a public park. During the autopsy, the medical examiner preserves the portion of her rib cage which sustained the fatal wound.
Two men are convicted of murder after a friend's testimony. Late a bomb kills the witness' father.

Janice Johnson was found dead at the foot of her basement stairs. Police in Nova Scotia had to unravel the circumstances surrounding Janice's death and answer the question: Was it an accident or murder?
A college student was found dead, and the evidence suggested he knew his killer.
The medical examiner ruled the death an accident, but the detectives investigating the case thought the evidence at the scene indicated otherwise.
In a rich suburb of Philadelphia, police were called to what appeared to be an accidental drowning.
When two women from the same town were murdered, police feared a serial killer was on the loose.

The murder of an American tourist in a Mexican resort draws law enforcement resources on both sides of the border. At first glance, the motive appears to be robbery, but careful analysis of the forensic evidence points to something more sinister.
Police are led to two suspects when a woman is found dead on a golf course.
When a pipe bomb rips through a rural home, police have no idea who is responsible. A 9-volt battery and the remnants of a mailing label ead investigators to the man who made the bomb.
Evidence leads to a killer when a teenager goes missing and a month later her body is found.

A 6-year-old girl ran and hid when she saw her grandmother being beaten to death, but the man followed, beat and assaulted her. She said the assailant was her uncle, who was later convicted. She recanted her testimony years later.
When a popular disc jockey was found murdered in a community garden, police swung into action.

In 1999, Susan Fassett was gunned down as she left her church choir practice in Poughkeepsie, NY. After clearing her husband, police turned their attention to Fred Andros, with whom Susan had an affair.
A man is gunned down and his wife injured. But then revealed that the wounds are self-inflicted.
It was a tragic twist of fate. Just days after a woman sold her home and moved to a modest trailer, a fire took both the trailer and her life. But the autopsy proved this was no accident.
Arsenic poisoning is found to be the cause of a woman's mysterious illness.

A 29-year-old woman is killed instantly when a bomb explodes in her home. The device is so powerful that it embedded shrapnel in houses across the street. The bomber had not only knowledge and skill, but also a motive for murder.
A man is murdered in his sleep, no fingerprints are left, a shoe impression leads to the killer.

Nancy Newman and her two daughters are found brutally murdered. The crime scene has no shortage of evidence, but investigators cannot find a conclusive link to their prime suspect. To solve the puzzle, an FBI analyst designs a unique experiment.
A shoe impression leads investigators on the right track to finding a killer.
In 1985, Julie Estes was kidnapped from the Southside convenience store where she worked. Her body was found the next day, but the killing went unsolved until 2003.
Chilling tale of debt and deceit when the head chef of a restaurant is found dead.
Haunted by the disappearance of her mother, a young woman undertakes an investigation of her own. In her mother's diary, she discovers a dark family secret that might explain the disappearance.
Serial arsonist leaves no evidence.

A woman was found dead on the bedroom floor of her apartment. The crime scene yielded little of value and investigators wondered if they would find enough evidence to make a case, much less catch a killer.
A woman's death is ruled a suicide, but forensics later prove her husband is a key suspect.

A woman's death in Pennsylvania triggers a homicide investigation into another woman's death in North Carolina. Faced with striking similarities, examiners must determine if their suspect's story about accidental drowning is all wet.
Three homicides on two continents have investigators on both sides of the Atlantic puzzled.

In 1996, Derrick Duehren returned to find his Oregon home burned to the ground. His wife's charred remains were later found in the rubble. Investigators set out to determine if it was an unfortunate accident or murder.
A woman was killed instantly when a bomb exploded in her home. Who planted the bomb?

In the summer of 1986, Kathleen Lipscomb's body was found on a deserted road outside of San Antonio. Months and years passed, but the crime was never solved. Finally, a private investigator discovered Kathleen's diary.
Fire wood found at a crime scene helps investigators locate a killer.

Emergency dispatch received a call from a man who said his girlfriend shot and killed herself. The autopsy revealed that the gunshot wound was not self-inflicted, and the evidence on her body would give police a golden opportunity to catch her killer.
A woman appears to have plunged her car into a creek. But investigators suspect foul play.
When a young fireman died from what appeared to be serious but undiagnosed heart disease, his family and friends had no proof of foul play.
When a successful stockbroker doesn't return home after a late shift, his wife reports him missing.
The prime suspect's driver's license was found at the scene of a brutal double homicide.
A retired police officer is found dead with a single gunshot wound to the head. His wife says the motive was robbery, but later tells police he committed suicide.
On October 15, 1985, two bomb explosions rocked Salt Lake City and resulted in two deaths. A third explosion occurred the next day; this time, the victim survived.
When a little girl got sick and died, investigators were stumped. Was it an accident or murder?
A couple is found dead in a car with broken windows but no shattered glass.
In 1984, a passerby finds the torso of a woman in a cardboard box. A forensic entomologist analyzes nearby insect activity to determine when the victim was killed.
Distinctive boots and a sweet tooth leads investigators to the killer of a WWII veteran.

In an affluent suburb of Philadelphia, police were called to the scene of what appeared to be an accidental drowning. The investigation gradually focused on one suspect who had more than a million reasons to want the victim dead.
Woman's apparent suicide proves to be murder when a hidden note is found in her china cabinet.

In 2006, Texas real estate agent Sarah Anne Walker was found brutally murdered in a model home. Weeks later, a witness came forward who may have seen the killer. Police used forensic hypnosis to help him recall every detail of the man's appearance.
Aspiring model's death points to her boyfriend who is soon cleared.

A young TV news producer is raped and murdered in her apartment. Police identify two suspects, but both are cleared of any wrongdoing. When the case stalls for more than a year, investigators turn to the Commonwealth of Virginia's DNA Databank.
When an off-duty policeman was shot dead, his fellow officers were determined to solve the crime.
When a woman and her daughter didn't return home from shopping, her husband directed police to a nearby mall. The child's body was found, but there was no sign of the wife.
To solve a triple homicide case, police had to delve into the world of high rollers.
The victim was well liked and successful, which made the brutality of the crime even harder to understand.
A young girl with no ID is found on an isolated farm but has mailbox and house keys.
In 1997, Kelly Eckart's car was found, with her belongings still in it, after she worked a late shift in Franklin, Indiana. Days later, her body was found in an isolated ravine.
A man denies killing a pedestrian in a hit-and-run, claiming he sold the car in question.

The 1987 disappearance of Houston resident Tracy Jo Shine is recalled. The investigation went cold until 2000 when a "cold case squad" learned that the woman's ex-boyfriend Michael Neal had bragged about killing her.
Who's right when a medical examiner and detectives disagree on the cause of death.

A suspicious fire sweeps through an apartment, killing two young women. The cause of the fire and the identity of the victims are unclear, but a closer look at the scene reveals something hidden in the ashes.
Boat passenger comes forward when the boat kills a young man in a hit-and-run.
How did the stalker obtain the security system code for his victim's home? How did he steal her personal photographs? Police needed answers and they found them in the most unlikely of places.
Crime scene where a woman is found dead on the bedroom floor yields few clues.
When Washington, DC is plagued by a series of arson fires — each started with the same type of incendiary device — it's up to forensic scientists to find the clues that lay in the ashes.
Police are suspicious of a mysterious car crash that kills a young man.
When a woman went missing, friends and family were determined to find her.

California police had several suspects in the robbery and brutal murder of an elderly couple. Ten years later, a determined forensic scientist used material from a dentist's office to uncover ballistic evidence that had been overlooked.
Evidence suggests the suspect of an unusual robbery-homicide case ran out of the house and not in.

A woman who was known to have suffered from depression apparently took her own life. But her sister told police that, a year before her death, she said if anything were to happen to her there would be a note in the china cabinet.
A wealthy man and his wife were attacked by three masked men outside their luxurious Louisiana home.
A murder trail turned cold, until police got a call from a woman whose husband, Gerald Powers, had a criminal past and a fondness for Chevy Berettas.
A bomb kills a man and a painstaking search yields tiny clues which precisely identify the killer.

When police doubt a young girl's story about being abused, fibers on her clothes help her case.
